passages.text: Introduction Our management’s discussion and analysis of financial condition and results of operations (MD&A) is provided to assist readers in understanding our performance, as reflected in the results of our operations, our financial condition and our cash flows and should be read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements and notes to consolidated financial statements included in Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data . The discussion in this MD&A contains forward-looking statements that involve substantial risks and uncertainties. Our objective is to also provide discussion of material events and uncertainties known to management that are reasonably likely to cause reported financial information not to be indicative of future results, which could differ materially from historical performance and from those anticipated in the forward-looking statements as a result of various factors such as those discussed in Item 1A. Risk Factors and Forward-looking statements and factors that may affect future results sections of this MD&A. A discussion regarding our financial condition and results of operations for fiscal 2025 compared to fiscal 2024 is presented below. A discussion regarding our financial condition and results of operations for fiscal 2024 compared to fiscal 2023 can be found under Item 7 of Part II of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, filed with the SEC on February 13, 2025 (our “2024 Annual Report”), which is available free of charge on the SEC’s website at www.sec.gov. With a legacy of nearly 75 years, we continue to pioneer ways to predict, prevent, detect, and treat animal illness, supporting those raising and caring for animals worldwide - from veterinarians and pet owners to livestock producers. We manage our operations through two geographic operating segments: the United States (U.S.) and International. Within each of these operating segments, we offer diverse products for both companion animals and livestock customers in order to capitalize on local and regional trends and customer needs. credit_strengths.text: Zoetis is a global animal health leader with roughly three hundred product lines sold in over one hundred countries, and its diversified companion animal and livestock portfolio underpins stable revenue and high operating margins well above the health care sector median, supporting strong internal cash generation.

Operating cash flow comfortably covers capital expenditure, leaving substantial free cash flow that covers gross interest expense many times over, while the current ratio and cash balance provide a solid liquidity cushion against near-term obligations.

key_risks.text: The risk factors highlight substantial risks and uncertainties that could cause reported results to differ materially from historical performance, and management explicitly cautions that past financial information may not be indicative of future results, which tempers confidence in cash-flow durability.

Gross debt increased sharply year over year, driven by long-term borrowings, and the maturity profile shows no repayment due in the next twelve months but meaningful maturities in the following years, requiring refinancing or cash deployment that could pressure liquidity.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is exceptionally strong and well above the sector median, while net leverage sits comfortably below the sector median and within the lowest indicative risk tier, leaving headroom before the next leverage threshold is breached.

Free cash flow to debt is solid and above the sector median, but shareholder distributions absorb most of that free cash flow, so debt reduction depends on disciplined capital allocation and sustained operating cash generation.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative financial risk profile is intermediate, with leverage in the strongest tier and cash-flow coverage in the second tier, and the Altman Z double prime zone is safe, supporting a stable credit trajectory absent a material earnings or cash-flow reversal.

Our forward view is that Zoetis can service its debt from internal cash flow, but the sharp debt increase and the absence of a tagged dividend figure limit visibility on total shareholder returns; we would monitor refinancing plans and distribution policy as key rating drivers.

credit_strengths.text: Zoetis 為全球動物保健領導者，擁有約三百條產品線，銷售遍及超過一百個國家，其多元化嘅伴侶動物及牲畜產品組合支撐穩定收入及遠高於醫療保健行業中位數嘅高營運利潤率，支持強勁嘅內部現金生成。
營運現金流足以輕鬆覆蓋資本開支，留下可觀嘅自由現金流，足以覆蓋總利息支出好多倍，而流動比率及現金結餘提供穩固嘅流動性緩衝，以應對短期債務。

key_risks.text: 風險因素強調重大風險及不確定性，可能導致報告業績與歷史表現存在重大差異，而管理層明確警告過往財務資料未必預示未來業績，令現金流持續性嘅信心受到影響。
總債務按年大幅增加，由長期借款帶動，而到期結構顯示未來十二個月並無還款到期，但隨後數年有顯著到期債務，需要再融資或現金調配，可能對流動性構成壓力。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率異常強勁，遠高於行業中位數，而淨槓桿率舒適地低於行業中位數，並處於最低指示性風險級別之內，在觸及下一個槓桿門檻之前仍有空間。
自由現金流對債務比率穩健，高於行業中位數，但股東分派吸收咗大部分自由現金流，因此債務減少取決於紀律性資本配置及持續營運現金生成。

overall_credit_view.text: 指示性財務風險狀況為中等，槓桿率處於最強級別，現金流覆蓋率處於第二級別，而 Altman Z 雙撇號區域為安全，支持穩定嘅信用軌跡，前提係並無重大盈利或現金流逆轉。
我哋嘅前瞻觀點係 Zoetis 可從內部現金流償付債務，但債務急增及並無標示股息數字限制咗對總股東回報嘅可見度；我哋會將再融資計劃及分派政策視為關鍵評級驅動因素並加以監察。
